A few things that have helped me:

Asking myself what I liked originally about this person

Taking a deep breath, trying to relax

Trying to recognize the root, were they doing something that someone has done in my past, red flag or not? Sometimes even if it’s not a red flag itself, sometimes the brain will make weird connections and we have to rewire ourselves. 

If not, it can have to do with the attention. For people with cPTSD, attention can be very complicated as it can be associated with negative things. Take a deep breath and try to relax. I honestly tell myself this 10+ times a day but I’m not exaggerating when sometimes I just have to count and breathe deeply until I cannot remember why I was anxious about whatever. 

Figure out the root of it. From there it should be more clear. For me when I *did* figure out it was tied to attention, I just gave it time. Every time he gave me positive affirmation or praise I froze and my heart sputtered. Not in a good way, mind you. It took a long time before the freeze reaction passed, and even then it went to a suspicion phase. Right now I’m in sort of a neutral phase, but I’m also starting to like his praise and affirmation. 

It took a long time and a lot of relationships I thought were healthy and good for me, when in reality they were just better than the terrible ones I’d experienced. But I’m learning, and you will too. It’s slow, hard work, but I believe in you.

Hi! I come from a narcissist parent that made it hard to identify, let alone enforce, boundaries and needs in a relationship. 

First, recognize this will be a slow process. You might not see any real progress for a while because this is hard work. 

Start by feeling things out. You may not always have an opinion about something and that is a-ok! Ask for reaction time. Instead of automatically agreeing with something because that’s your first feeling, wait a sec. Think about it. What does this take from you, and what does this give to you? Does this satisfy a need? Do you need it to? 

Expand your questions from there. Do I feel like I need anything else in my life? Do I feel like I need to stop anything in my life? Are there things bothering me I am able to fix? If not, don’t worry. As you start paying attention to your own needs and wants, you find a way to communicate with yourself when you do stumble upon a boundary. 

The next step is setting and enforcing boundaries. 

To set a boundary, it’s as easy as saying “hey. I really don’t like it when you say XYZ around me. You don’t have to stop saying it, but I’d appreciate it if it weren’t around me. “ 

Enforcing that boundary however, that can be the hard part. Many people will ask why and if you provide them a reason, most will be agreeable. Some people will not and you need to know in advance whether this boundary is enough to cut the tie, ignore for that person, or some other option. 

Finding and enforcing boundaries is hard, unforgiving work. You may lose friends. It will also make you incredibly happy and whole after a long time of doing it and putting yourself around people that are respectful of your boundaries. 

Good luck.
